summary: The START-NEW-GAME scripted entry narration is a SINGLE modal message page shown on dungeon entry (game_state=5, wmaze-internal): 'APPROACHING THE GATE WITH CONFIDENCE, YOU KNOW IF THINGS GET TOO HAIRY YOU CAN ALWAYS TURN AND RUN BACK OUT...'. It is msg.dbs IDs 10010/10011/10012 (the multi-line message renderer loads consecutive IDs starting at 10010 until it hits an empty/absent record at 10013). Dismissed by ENTER, which then begins a scripted forward gate-walk (each subsequent ENTER = one forward step; ~10-13 taps reach the closed inner gate, where ENTER yields the 'HMMMM...' bump message = msg 10020). The '~10 ENTER taps' in the prior finding were the walk steps, NOT 10 message pages. CRITICAL #025 UPDATE: the msg.dbs high range (>=718) is NOW fully decodable in extracted/messages/msg.json (4562 IDs >=718 decoded, up to id 18961) via the bank-structured decoder in packages/parser/src/formats/message-db.ts. The narration IDs (10010-10012, bank 20, rangeIndex 112) decode VERBATIM-MATCHING the on-screen render. #025 is NOT a blocker; recommended port path is DECODE-FROM-MSG (no fixture-capture needed). Caller: wmaze msg_show_short_in_window (wmaze file ~0x5943, return offset CS:0x9eac = file 0x5948 via the 0x4564 delta law).

findings.claim: The scripted entry narration for the START-NEW-GAME (default Bane scenario) flow is exactly ONE modal page of THREE lines, verbatim: line1='APPROACHING THE GATE WITH CONFIDENCE,', line2='YOU KNOW IF THINGS GET TOO HAIRY YOU ' (note trailing space), line3='^CAN ALWAYS TURN AND RUN BACK OUT...'. The leading '^' on line3 is the engine's anchored-x format code (per msg_window_draw_text_wrapped @ wmaze 0x57a8 which handles '$'=newline and '^'=anchored-x), not literal text. The text is drawn into the bottom message window (screen band y>=176).

evidence.details: Screenshot /tmp/wiz6-narr2-00.png (saved during the drive) shows the three lines in the bottom message window over the live dungeon view with the 3-member party panel (THESUS/TEMPEST/LYSANDR). msg.json IDs 10010='APPROACHING THE GATE WITH CONFIDENCE,', 10011='YOU KNOW IF THINGS GET TOO HAIRY YOU ', 10012='^CAN ALWAYS TURN AND RUN BACK OUT...' match the render character-for-character.

findings.claim: The narration loads msg.dbs IDs 10010, 10011, 10012 (and probes 10013 which is empty/absent = the terminator). Captured by tracing load_msg_into_buf (wroot image 0x75b) during dungeon entry: 4 hits with msg_id args 10010,10011,10012,10013, all from the same caller return offset 0x9eac. The message renderer walks consecutive IDs from a start ID until an empty record terminates. Same pattern for the wall-bump 'HMMMM...' message: ID 10020 (+ 10021 terminator).

evidence.details: traceSet((0x1a8<<4)+0x75b); on dungeon-entry ENTER: 10 total load_msg hits; the narration-range (>=10000) ones were msg_id=10010/10011/10012/10013 all with stack[0] (return offset) = 0x9eac. The other 6 hits at this commit: 1300-1303 ('PRESS'/'RETURN'/'FOR'/'OPTIONS' = status-bar hint, ret 0x84f) and 2000/2001 (party-panel chrome glyphs, ret 0x4e9a/0x4ea8). 13 forward-walk taps later: msg_id=10020/10021 (the 'HMMMM...' wall bump).

findings.claim: TODO #025 (high-range msg.dbs ID->section/offset decode) is RESOLVED for the purposes of this port. The current extracted/messages/msg.json decodes the full range: 4712 of 5161 indexed IDs have decodedText, including 4562 IDs >=718 (max decoded id = 18961). The bank-structured decoder (packages/parser/src/formats/message-db.ts: parse ranges from msg.hdr as packed=(bank_idx<<8)|id_span, then walk id_span+1 consecutive records per range) handles bank 20. So porting the narration does NOT require any further #025 work. Recommended port path: DECODE-FROM-MSG (read IDs 10010-10012 from msg.json), NOT fixture-capture-as-strings. (Fixture capture remains a viable fallback — /tmp/wiz6-narr2-00.png is committed-ready ground truth for a pixel-parity test of the narration page.)

evidence.details: python3 over extracted/messages/msg.json: with-decodedText=4712, decoded-id-range 100..18961, decoded-with-id>=718 = 4562. IDs 10010-10012 present with correct text. The prior 'IDs 0..717 only' note (carried in wbase-add-party-member.json and TODO #025) is STALE — the extractor was extended since.

findings.claim: Flow: the narration page appears IMMEDIATELY on the dungeon-entry frame (game_state already = 5, dungeon view + party panel already live, party already positioned at the entrance) — the message is shown BEFORE/AT the party-at-entrance frame, gating only input. ONE ENTER dismisses the text page; subsequent ENTERs drive a scripted forward gate-walk (each ENTER = one forward step). It is a single modal box, ENTER-dismissed; not a data-driven list of multiple narration pages in this path (only the one 10010-block fires).

evidence.details: Frame-by-frame screenshots: page0 (pre-extra-ENTER) shows the narration; after 1 ENTER the text is gone and the view advances; taps 1-12 = forward walk through the corridor (no further text); tap 13 = inner closed gate -> 'HMMMM...' (msg 10020). game_state stayed 5 throughout. The narration is wmaze-internal (matches prior maze-start-new-game.json).

findings.claim: The narration is displayed by msg_show_short_in_window (wmaze 0x58ed, 'Opens a small window, draws message, waits, closes'). The load_msg_into_buf calls return to wmaze CS:0x9eac, which is wmaze file offset 0x9eac - 0x4564 = 0x5948 (per the wmaze 0x4564 overlay delta), inside the 0x58ed..0x5a28 function. wmaze runtime CS observed = 0x6b91, DGROUP phys base = 0xffa0 (anchor) in this session.

evidence.details: All four 10010-10013 load_msg hits had trace stack[0] (return offset within wmaze CS) = 0x9eac. wmaze.ovr is 0x973d bytes; 0x9eac > 0x973d so the delta law applies: 0x9eac - 0x4564 = 0x5948, which falls inside msg_show_short_in_window (0x58ed-0x5a28) per docs/re/wmaze-functions.md. The CALL instruction is ~5 bytes before, ~0x5943. NOTE: the routine that DECIDES to show 10010 on dungeon entry (the trigger) was not separately localized — only the display routine.

findings.claim: The narration text page itself plays NO dedicated sound. play_sound_entry (wroot 0xaaa) fires during dungeon entry, but those calls come from other call sites (sound IDs 3 from ret 0x4fcd; 10/11/12 from ret 0x4679 = gate-walk footstep/movement SFX), NOT from the narration display routine (ret 0x9eac). So a faithful port does not need to play a sound when showing the narration box.

evidence.details: traceSet((0x1a8<<4)+0xaaa) over the dungeon-entry ENTER: 12 hits, none with return offset 0x9eac. sound_id args: 0x3 x3 (ret 0x4fcd), then 0xa/0xb/0xc (ret 0x4679) — these accompany the scripted walk/gate, not the text box.

wroot resident CS = 0x1a8; a wroot image offset X is traceable at linear (0x1a8<<4)+X. wmaze runtime CS = 0x6b91 this session.

Trace-record stack[] = top 8 words at ss:sp captured AT the breakpoint; for a cdecl fn at entry, stack[0]=return offset, stack[1]=arg0, stack[2]=arg1. (Re-reading ss:sp from RAM after traceDrain returns stale/zero data — use the record's stack[] words.)
